questions.source_raw: During a week-long field test for an autonomous hospital delivery cart, engineers notice that the cart enters the final straight section of the corridor at \(4.8\,\text{m/s}\) while a constant braking system can provide only \(1.6\,\text{m/s}^2\) of deceleration. The cart is \(6.5\,\text{m}\) from a sealed lab door, and the faculty supervisor wants a written justification rather than a single numerical answer. Explain whether the cart stops before it reaches the door, and show how the relevant kinematics relationship supports your conclusion.

questions.source_raw: A biomedical sensor package is launched straight upward from the roof of a clinic with an initial speed of \(18\,\text{m/s}\). Ignore air resistance unless a part states otherwise. (a) Determine the time it takes the package to reach its maximum height. (b) Which statement best describes the package's acceleration while it is in flight?
questions.stem: A biomedical sensor package is launched straight upward from the roof of a clinic with an initial speed of \(18\,\text{m/s}\). Ignore air resistance unless a part states otherwise.

parts.stem: Determine the time it takes the package to reach its maximum height.
Which statement best describes the package's acceleration while it is in flight?

options.text: The acceleration is zero at the top of the path.
The acceleration is downward and approximately \(9.8\,\text{m/s}^2\) throughout the flight.
The acceleration points upward while the package rises and downward while it falls.
The acceleration decreases linearly to zero as the package approaches the top.
